summary: Make timing a property of paths through a circuit, with the longest path selected by summation rather than by appearance.
objective: Build a combinational circuit in space where each gate carries a delay and the critical path is computed and highlighted.
intent_signals: Show which path through a circuit sets its delay.
Explain propagation delay and contamination delay in a 3D circuit.
example_prompts: Build a gate network with per-gate delays and a highlighted critical path.
Show how changing one gate delay moves the critical path.
negative_signals: Not a transistor-level or SPICE timing model; delays here are declared per gate.
Not a synthesis or place-and-route tool.
not_for: Not a transistor-level or SPICE timing model; delays here are declared per gate.
Not a synthesis or place-and-route tool.

entities.name: Gate blocks
entities.guidance: Give each gate a body with labelled input and output faces and a visible delay value, so timing data belongs to the object.

entities.name: Wire routing
entities.guidance: Route wires with distinguishable paths and junction beads; a wire whose route is ambiguous makes a path highlight meaningless.

entities.name: Path highlight
entities.guidance: Highlight the selected path as a connected chain from an input to the output with a running delay sum shown along it.

state_contract.model: A directed acyclic gate network with finite nonnegative per-gate propagation and contamination delays satisfying contamination at most propagation, path enumeration, circuit propagation delay as the maximum path sum and contamination delay as the minimum path sum. A graph with no input-to-output path reports that no path exists rather than a zero delay.
state_contract.authority: The network and its delay values are authoritative; every highlighted path and every reported number is recomputed from them.
actions: Edit a gate delay and rerun the path analysis.
Step along the critical path gate by gate.
Toggle between propagation and contamination path highlighting.

invariants: The reported circuit propagation delay equals the sum along the highlighted path, and the two update together.
Contamination delay is a minimum over paths and is never larger than the reported propagation delay.
A cycle in the network is rejected: this analysis applies to combinational logic only.
motion_guidance: Animate signal validity sweeping along the path in delay-proportional time, and label the time scale as illustrative.
Do not animate all wires simultaneously with the same speed; that hides the very difference being measured.
known_limits: Delays are declared values, not measured device parameters, and wire delay is ignored unless modelled explicitly.
Path enumeration grows quickly with reconvergent fanout; large networks need a proper timing algorithm.

Structural path sums are bounds: a path that cannot be sensitised by any input pattern still appears in the enumeration, so the validity animation illustrates a bound rather than an observed transition time.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

claims.statement: The propagation delay of a combinational gate is an upper bound on the delay from valid inputs to valid outputs, while the contamination delay is a lower bound on the delay from an invalid input to an invalid output.
claims.scope: Definitions as taught for gate-level timing; specific values are technology dependent.

source_refs.locator: 3.1 slides, propagation and contamination delay definitions

claims.statement: The propagation delay of a circuit is found by summing gate propagation delays along each input-to-output path and taking the largest such path delay.
claims.scope: Combinational networks without cycles; wire delay is neglected in this rule as stated.

source_refs.locator: 3.1 slides, computing circuit t_PD from path sums

object_craft.structure: Extruded gate bodies with recognisable silhouettes per function plus a data plate showing the delay value.
object_craft.material: Neutral matte gate bodies so the critical path accent stands out; label plates opaque for legibility.
object_craft.articulation: None. Gates are static; only highlight and labels change.

object_craft.structure: Rounded orthogonal routes with bridges at crossings so two wires never appear to merge.
object_craft.material: Two-value wire palette for logic zero and one, with a separate reserved accent for the highlighted path.
object_craft.articulation: Signal validity travels as a moving segment along the wire during animation.

physical_contract.scope: Discrete logic and timing arithmetic; no physical layout or electrical simulation.
checks: The highlighted path sum equals the reported circuit delay.
Increasing a delay on the critical path increases the reported delay by the same amount.
